node.text: LESSON 192
get by
When there isn't enough room to get by two people talking to each other in a narrow corridor, what can you say?
When there isn't ..., I can say "Excuse me, can I get by, please?".
How little sleep can you get by on each night without suffering from tiredness?
I can get by on ... without ...
Give me an example of the word "regardless", please.
He took part in the rugby match regardless of his injuries.
make your way
Would you be able to make your way from here to the coast (the capital etc.) without consulting any kind of map?
If you felt your hearing was starting to deteriorate, would you visit your doctor first or consult a specialist immediately?
What do we mean by a trail in the countryside?
By ..., we mean a path or track leading through the countryside that people can walk along.
Is it a pretty straightforward process to renew an expired passport in your country?
What do you have to do?
You have to ...
Name a food you definitely wouldn't eat if it was past its expiry date.
A food ... is ...
Which institutions undertake responsibility for upholding the law in a country?
The police and the courts undertake ...
Why do elderly people sometimes take a nap in the middle of the day?
Elderly ... because they get tired easily.
give in
Have you ever given in a piece of homework knowing it was absolutely awful?
Do universities normally get students to submit assignments online?
Yes, ...
What's the maximum daily amount you can withdraw from your account using a cash machine?
The maximum ...
Who's in charge of the household budget in your family?
... in charge of ...

We generally use the word "storey" when we are referring to the architecture or structure of a building, whereas we use "floor" when talking about the different levels within a building. For example, we would say "Mr Brown's cousin lives on the fifth floor of a ten-storey block of flats".
Would you like to work on the top floor of a 30-storey skyscraper?
Why or why not?
mother tongue
Do you think someone with a talent for learning languages can attain the same level of ability in a foreign language as they have in their mother tongue?
What would I mean if I said "The wedding day went like clockwork"?
If you ..., you'd mean that every part of the wedding day happened on time and in the way it had been planned.
Do airline passengers on long flights suffer discomfort if they don't have adequate leg room?
Yes, airline passengers ...
Are accidents in the workplace often a consequence of inadequate safety measures?
Yes, ...
Excluding travel and accommodation costs, about how much money do you need to get by each week?
Excluding ..., I need ...
Is there any type of food you exclude from your diet to avoid problems with digestion?
Do airlines give their crew members training in how to cope with aggressive passengers?
Yes, ...
When does a dog growl?
A dog growls when it wants to show aggression.
in the event of
If a country had no military, would it be completely helpless in the event of an attack?
Yes, ...
Give me another example of "in the event of".
In the event of an emergency, please alert a member of staff immediately.
join in
Why do some children at primary school find it hard to join in with others in the playground?
Some ... they aren't used to interacting with other children, they're shy etc.

The verb "instruct" means "teach" but is generally used to describe teaching someone how to perform an activity. For example, we can say "The staff were instructed on what to do in the event of a fire".
Do you think you'd enjoy the job of driving instructor?
Why or why not?
How do we moisten an envelope so that it sticks when we close it?
We moisten ... by licking the edge that folds down.
Are there occasional outbreaks of flu in the world that cause massive numbers of deaths?
Yes, ...
Give me another example of the word "occasional", please.
I have the occasional pint of beer at the weekend.
When swimming in a lake, why should we enter the water carefully rather than just plunge in?
When ..., ... because the water may be too shallow, or there may be rocks close to the surface of the water.
Why are visitors often asked to register at reception when they enter the premises of a big business?
Visitors are ... for security reasons.
Do you think your parents would describe you as having been a troublesome child?
Why does a person's philosophy on life often alter significantly as they get older?
A person's ...
Word-Building Exercise 1
Change each word in brackets so that it fits correctly in its sentence.
She was (luck) to win the game.
Answer: lucky
Anne's (face) features are so striking she could be a model if she wanted.
If this company hopes to grow, there'll need to be an (expand) in the range of products we offer.
This magazine is currently the only (publish) that makes any profit for the business.
It's hard to know what the (significant) of this latest decision will be.
The national TV station was praised for its detailed (cover) of events during the war.
The phone (direct) is published online to save printing costs.
Peter's quiet in the classroom but he's a lot more (talk) outside.
I'm not sure (global) has been good for the economy of my country.
Investing money in the (preserve) of this college building is an excellent idea.
Her sudden (declare) of love took him completely by surprise.
I'm sorry, but I really can't see the (relevant) of what you're saying. What's it got to do with the topic we're discussing?
Life today is not (compare) to life a thousand years ago; it's so much easier now.
The sales assistants in that store can be very (persuade), so be careful!
I've had a terribly (problem) day so far. Let's hope it gets better.
I'm not sure whether the price he's quoted me for the job is (include) of tax or not.
Dictation 134

It was by no means/ a desperate time for her/ after the divorce;/ in fact, she coped very well indeed./ Neither of us can stand/ using the vacuum cleaner,/ so what's stopping us/ paying someone to do the household chores/ while we're at work?/ Let's hope the bridegroom/ gives a decent speech./ Richard glanced up/ and was thrilled to spot/ the marvellous city lights ahead./ It had been a long, tedious train journey,/ but soon he'd be home again,/ catching up with family and friends./ This sweater I knitted is fabulous/ but slightly too large./ Can I deliberately shrink it/ in the washing machine?/ Children often go through/ a stubborn phase/ when they rebel/ against their parents' authority./ Perceive, loathe, overdraft,/ neutral, leisure, pursue.
